title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Sealed when coverage, with one-click branch insertion
summary: A coverage CodeLens above every `when` on a sealed hierarchy or enum: see missing branches before the compiler does, and insert them all in one click. Desktop and vscode.dev.

highlights.title: Sealed When Coverage
highlights.description: Every `when` over a sealed class, sealed interface, or enum gets a lens: ✓ 3/3 branches when exhaustive, ⚠ 2/3 branches with the missing names when incomplete, and `else covers N remaining` when an else hides unhandled subtypes. No compiler, no waiting.

highlights.title: Insert Missing Branches
highlights.description: Click an incomplete lens and the missing branches appear with placeholder bodies, spelled the way your file already writes them: bare names for objects and enum entries, `is` for classes, same qualification style. The cursor lands on the first inserted stub, ready to fill in.

highlights.title: Truthful by Design
highlights.description: When a branch is ambiguous or unresolved, the lens stays silent instead of guessing. Kotlin 2.1 guard branches (`is A if cond ->`) are recognized and excluded from exhaustiveness, matching the language spec.

sections.heading: Features
bullets: Coverage CodeLens above `when` expressions over sealed classes, sealed interfaces, and enums, with exact missing-branch names in the title.
One-click insertion of missing branches with kind-aware spelling and placeholder bodies, on desktop and vscode.dev alike.
Toggle with kotlinJump.sealedWhenCoverage; analysis steps and skip reasons are traced as [SealedWhen] lines in the Kotlin Jump output channel.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: UpperCamelCase enum entries are now indexed correctly; they used to produce phantom one-letter symbols in Go to Symbol or be dropped entirely.
Fixed the column of enum entries with constructor arguments, which produced overlapping semantic tokens in the editor.
